findings.problem: Most of the Big Idea walks through the sermon in order, one section after another ("Then He asks...", "Then Jesus tells them a parable...", "Then Jesus talks about trees..."), and restates the verses without saying what they mean. Lines 4 and 5 are the clearest cases. Line 4 repeats Luke 6:39-42 (the blind leading the blind, a disciple and his teacher, the speck and the beam) and line 5 repeats Luke 6:44-45 (a tree known by its fruit, the overflow of the heart). Neither line says what these sayings teach or how they connect to the rest of the sermon. Only lines 2, 3 and 6 say what the passage means.

rule.text: A real summary of what the passage means, not a retelling of the verses.

findings.problem: The Big Idea leaves out the opening of the passage completely. In Luke 6:17-19 the crowds come from Judea, Jerusalem, Tyre and Sidon to hear Jesus and be healed, and power comes from Him and heals them all. The rest of the Big Idea covers the sermon itself (Luke 6:20-49).
findings.question: In a Sermons passage, does "It covers the whole passage" mean the Big Idea must also mention the story around the sermon (here the crowd and the healings in Luke 6:17-19), or is it enough to cover the sermon?
